meta.basis: 100 synthetic domain validation cases rewritten from public internet research about residential inspection system defects, water intrusion, roof and sewer scope limitations, electrical and HVAC safety, WDI conditions, pool/deck/chimney hazards, and insurance underwriting friction.
meta.warning: These are internet-researched synthetic cases, not verified customer interviews, legal advice, lending advice, insurance advice, or repair estimates.

cases.sourceBasis: Roof and general inspection standards treat active roof leakage and visible flashing defects as material system issues rather than cosmetic age comments.
cases.deal: Conventional buyer has seven inspection days left on a 1990s two-story home.
findings: active roof leak at rear bedroom ceiling
cases.requiredGate: quote-needed roofing scope and photo evidence
cases.riskIfWrong: The ask may become an unsupported roof replacement demand instead of a defensible leak repair or credit.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA roof flashing guidance links failed roof penetrations to water intrusion and downstream damage, making source control more important than repainting stains.
cases.deal: Inspection contingency is open but seller says the ceiling stain was already painted once.
findings: open sealant gap at skylight flashing
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer could accept paint touchup while the leak source remains active.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection standards distinguish observed active leakage from merely estimating roof life expectancy.
cases.deal: Buyer sent a broad roof replacement request after a dry inspection.
findings: roof is 18 years old but dry
expectedLeadScope: roof certification or roofer evaluation only
cases.requiredGate: age-alone is not a replacement basis
cases.riskIfWrong: The system validates an overbroad ask that a seller can reject as age-based preference.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance underwriting sources show roof age and remaining useful life can be a deal risk even when the report does not call for immediate failure.
cases.deal: AS IS contract; buyer cannot bind insurance until four-point items are reviewed.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may discover after the inspection period that the roof prevents affordable coverage.

cases.sourceBasis: Roof penetrations, flashing, and attic staining are system clues that require source diagnosis before price negotiation.
cases.deal: Remote buyer needs a concise high-risk summary before deciding whether to fly in.
findings: attic sheathing dark staining near bath vent
improper bathroom exhaust termination into attic
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer cannot separate a ventilation moisture issue from a roof leak and may ask for the wrong repair.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards include gutters, downspouts, and drainage where they can adversely affect the structure.
cases.deal: Inspection happened during rain and water was observed at the foundation line.
cases.riskIfWrong: The request may treat crawlspace moisture as isolated instead of addressing roof runoff feeding the problem.

cases.sourceBasis: Roof leak risk rises when damaged flashing or roof covering defects are paired with interior moisture indicators.
cases.persona: Team lead reviewing junior agent packet
cases.deal: Junior agent drafted a request for every roof note on a 42-page report.
findings: missing shingles at plumbing vent slope
water stain in attic below same slope
minor nail pops on porch shingles
cases.riskIfWrong: A valid leak ask gets diluted by minor maintenance items.

cases.sourceBasis: HUD/FHA collateral guidance and public roof standards treat roof serviceability differently from cosmetic finish.
cases.deal: FHA buyer has inspection findings before appraisal is complete.
findings: active roof leak over kitchen light
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may imply a seller credit is enough when repair completion could affect financing.

cases.sourceBasis: Roof water entry around chimneys should be separated from fireplace flue safety and masonry scope.
cases.deal: General inspection and chimney scan produce overlapping but different defects.
findings: cracked clay flue tile reported by chimney camera
cases.requiredGate: split roof leak from chimney fire-safety scope
cases.riskIfWrong: The ask may use one trade quote to cover two distinct hazards and become indefensible.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance and inspection guidance treat roof damage, active leaks, and age-driven underwriting as separate negotiation tracks.
cases.deal: Buyer has an insurance quote pending and option period ends tomorrow.
findings: buyer wants seller to file insurance claim
cases.requiredGate: do not assume carrier coverage or claim path
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet could direct the seller into an insurance claim strategy outside the buyer's evidence base.

cases.sourceBasis: Sewer scope standards report root intrusion, offsets, standing water, and blockages as material defects in the lateral line.
cases.deal: Sewer scope returned before the Colorado objection deadline.
findings: tree root intrusion at clay sewer joints
scope could not pass beyond 62 feet
expectedLeadScope: complete sewer scope or repair quote
cases.requiredGate: sewer video and plumber quote needed
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may negotiate a small cleaning credit when a blocked or broken lateral could be a major repair.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA sanitary sewer overflow guidance identifies roots, grease, cracks, and stormwater infiltration as overflow and backup causes.
cases.deal: Seller says the basement floor drain has only backed up once after a storm.
findings: floor drain backup residue in basement
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer could miss a private lateral defect until sewage backs up after closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Sewer scope standards treat incomplete access or blocked camera travel as a limitation that should not be converted into a clean bill of health.
cases.deal: Listing side claims the sewer passed because the first 30 feet looked clean.
findings: sewer camera stopped at heavy obstruction
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet could falsely treat a limited scope as a pass and leave the buyer with unknown lateral risk.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA septic homeowner guidance emphasizes drainfield protection, maintenance, and avoiding root or vehicle damage.
cases.deal: VA buyer is under contract on acreage with a private septic system.
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may underplay a sanitation issue that can affect loan approval and post-close usability.

cases.sourceBasis: Septic and sewer guidance separate public lateral defects from private onsite wastewater failures, which need different specialists and responsibilities.
cases.deal: Older home converted from septic to public sewer decades ago.
findings: public sewer lateral has root intrusion
seller unsure if tank was filled
cases.riskIfWrong: A single generic plumbing request may miss buried tank liability and lateral repair responsibility.

cases.sourceBasis: Sewer scope standards list offsets and separated lines as defects distinct from routine drain cleaning.
cases.deal: Seller offers to snake the line but refuses a repair credit.
findings: offset clay sewer joint over one quarter inch
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer accepts temporary cleaning for a pipe defect likely to recur.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA overflow guidance treats fats, wipes, and inadequate maintenance as blockage contributors, but a buyer request still needs property-specific evidence.
cases.deal: Buyer requests full sewer replacement after a slow-drain note without a scope.
findings: buyer asks for full lateral replacement
cases.riskIfWrong: The request overclaims a hidden sewer defect without video or plumber support.

cases.sourceBasis: Sewer scope findings need usable video, distance markers, and defect labels before being turned into a dollar ask.
cases.deal: Team lead is reviewing a packet for a 1950s bungalow.
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may ask for an invented sewer credit without knowing repair location or method.

cases.sourceBasis: Private sewer laterals can be outside a standard home inspection scope, so missing a recommended ancillary scope is a validation failure.
cases.deal: Inspector wants to test whether the product flags ancillary sewer scope opportunities.
cases.requiredGate: ancillary inspection prompt, not repair demand
cases.riskIfWrong: The tool either misses a major hidden system risk or overstates a defect not yet inspected.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA septic maintenance guidance points to records, tank condition, and drainfield function as decision-critical for rural purchases.
cases.deal: Cash buyer can close quickly but has no lender forcing septic documentation.
cases.requiredGate: cash buyer still needs sanitation risk gate
cases.riskIfWrong: The system may treat cash as low-risk and fail to surface a costly onsite wastewater issue.

cases.sourceBasis: Foundation inspection guidance distinguishes small cosmetic cracks from cracks paired with displacement, moisture, or framing symptoms.
cases.deal: Option period ends in 36 hours on a slab home in expansive-soil market.
findings: diagonal interior cracks at multiple doors
front bedroom door out of square
cases.riskIfWrong: A generic handyman repair ask could miss structural movement and option-period leverage.

cases.sourceBasis: Building America and FEMA water-management guidance emphasizes grading, gutters, and foundation drainage before interior finish repair.
cases.deal: Basement finish is new, but inspection found wet foundation corners.
findings: moisture meter elevated at finished wall
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may negotiate floor repair while water continues entering behind the wall.

cases.sourceBasis: Crawlspace inspection guidance treats active water penetration, wood contact, and compromised framing as material structure concerns.
cases.deal: Due diligence period is expensive and buyer needs a go/no-go recommendation.
findings: wood joist ends damp near foundation
cases.riskIfWrong: The tool may minimize crawlspace water that can drive rot, insects, and structural damage.

cases.sourceBasis: Foundation drainage resources link saturated soil and hydrostatic pressure to basement and crawlspace moisture defects.
cases.deal: Seller countered with a dehumidifier instead of exterior drainage work.
findings: sump pump cycles during dry weather
cases.requiredGate: seller counter does not solve source
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may accept an appliance instead of resolving foundation water loading.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards report observed indications of possible foundation movement but do not provide engineering conclusions.
cases.deal: Agent draft says the house has structural failure without an engineer report.
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet creates liability by stating an expert conclusion the evidence does not support.

cases.sourceBasis: Below-grade moisture guidance separates surface drainage fixes from structural foundation repairs.
cases.deal: Spring thaw revealed seepage at the basement stairwell.
findings: settled exterior concrete slopes toward door
foundation wall has hairline cracks only
older but working freezer in basement
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer either over-asks for foundation replacement or under-asks by treating seepage as cosmetic.

cases.sourceBasis: Crawlspace standards flag wood near soil and active water because they can create structural and WDI conditions.
cases.deal: VA buyer on a rural pier-and-beam property.
findings: wood lattice and debris touching crawlspace soil
cases.riskIfWrong: Product could miss the overlap between moisture, pests, structure, and VA repair pressure.

cases.sourceBasis: Foundation crack guidance treats horizontal or bowing wall symptoms differently from shrinkage cracks.
cases.deal: Older basement home has a seller-provided waterproofing invoice.
findings: horizontal crack in block foundation wall
wall bowing visible along garage side
cases.requiredGate: structural quote separate from waterproofing receipt
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may accept a waterproofing invoice for a structural wall movement problem.

cases.sourceBasis: Drainage guidance says lots should move water away from foundations; flat or reverse grade creates repeat intrusion risk.
cases.deal: Builder says grading will settle and can be handled after closing.
findings: yard grade slopes toward slab patio door
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer closes on a drainage defect with limited leverage after occupancy.

cases.sourceBasis: Foundation and crawlspace inspection limits require noting inaccessible areas instead of assuming hidden structure is acceptable.
cases.deal: Raised home has stored items blocking most crawlspace access.
findings: crawlspace access blocked by stored lumber
visible sill plate has fungal-like staining
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet could treat inaccessible structural areas as cleared.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC aluminum wiring guidance recommends expert evaluation and recognizes warning signs like warm devices, odors, and flickering.
cases.deal: 1970s home has branch wiring concerns during inspection.
cases.riskIfWrong: The request may treat aluminum wiring as a cosmetic age note instead of fire and insurability risk.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC and inspection guidance warn untrained people not to inspect or repair hazardous wiring, making DIY seller repairs a poor substitute.
cases.deal: Seller proposes to have a handyman fix electrical items before closing.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may rely on unqualified electrical work that increases shock, fire, and closing risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance underwriting sources commonly scrutinize electrical system age, panel condition, exposed wiring, and active hazards in four-point reviews.
cases.deal: AS IS buyer needs a four-point inspection for insurance before the deadline.
cases.requiredGate: insurance and electrician confirmation before send
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may negotiate a minor repair while the carrier refuses coverage.

cases.sourceBasis: Public electrical risk sources identify Zinsco/Sylvania-Zinsco panels as high-risk underwriting and safety issues requiring electrician evaluation.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to waive repairs to keep the deal competitive.
findings: seller says panel has never tripped
expectedExclusions: seller says panel has never tripped
cases.requiredGate: do not rely on no-failure history
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may let the buyer waive a major fire and insurance red flag as if it were normal age.

cases.sourceBasis: General inspection standards require reporting electrical defects observed at accessible systems while avoiding code-inspector overreach.
cases.deal: Agent draft cites code violations without permit or electrician review.
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet creates brokerage liability by calling code conclusions instead of requesting qualified evaluation.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC aluminum wiring guidance distinguishes proper remediation from casual pigtailing or device replacement.
cases.deal: Buyer asks seller to replace every outlet after aluminum wiring note.
findings: aluminum branch wiring at some receptacles
cases.requiredGate: remediation method must be specified by qualified electrician
cases.riskIfWrong: The ask may request a cosmetic outlet swap that fails to address actual aluminum wiring risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Electrical panel hazards and obsolete panel brands are treated as different from simple capacity preferences.
cases.deal: Investor wants seller to fund a 200-amp upgrade for a future remodel.
findings: one open junction box in attic
cases.riskIfWrong: Product turns inspection leverage into remodel funding and loses seller credibility.

cases.sourceBasis: Electrical safety evidence should prioritize live exposed conductors, missing covers, and shock hazards over cosmetic fixture preferences.
cases.deal: Buyer is nervous after seeing many low-cost electrical notes.
findings: exposed live wire in attic light box
cases.riskIfWrong: A serious shock hazard gets buried inside cosmetic electrical cleanup.

cases.sourceBasis: Four-point underwriting reviews electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and roof systems, so an electrical defect can be a closing condition beyond repair cost.
cases.deal: Insurance binder is required before clear-to-close.
findings: buyer asks for seller credit only
cases.riskIfWrong: A negotiated credit may not help if the insurer requires repair before issuing coverage.

cases.sourceBasis: Electrical defects near water or exterior conditions create higher shock risk and should not be treated as generic handyman items.
cases.deal: Pool inspection and general inspection overlap at the equipment pad.
cases.requiredGate: pool electrician or qualified contractor review
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may lump electrocution risk with cosmetic pool maintenance.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC furnace guidance emphasizes annual qualified inspection, clear venting, and carbon monoxide risk for fuel-fired heating systems.
cases.deal: Inspection found heat but flagged combustion safety concerns.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer could accept a maintenance cleaning while a carbon monoxide hazard remains.

cases.sourceBasis: ENERGY STAR HVAC guidance links poor airflow, refrigerant charge, and duct condition to performance and system life, requiring contractor diagnosis.
cases.deal: Summer inspection found inadequate cooling in a desert market.
findings: AC supply air temperature split low
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may demand a full system replacement before confirming duct or charge defects.

cases.sourceBasis: HVAC maintenance guidance treats dirt and neglect as causes of failure but still requires distinguishing maintenance from nonfunctional equipment.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for a new condenser after inspection noted deferred maintenance.
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller can reject the request because the evidence supports service, not replacement.

cases.sourceBasis: Fuel-fired appliance and chimney/flue safety sources treat blocked or damaged venting as life-safety risk.
cases.deal: FHA buyer with appraisal pending and furnace concern visible in inspection.
findings: gas furnace vent disconnected at draft hood
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may frame a life-safety venting defect as an optional credit.

cases.sourceBasis: HVAC quality guidance warns oversized or short-cycling systems can perform poorly despite being relatively new.
cases.deal: Newer HVAC system was installed without permits or load documentation.
cases.riskIfWrong: The system may assume newer equipment is low-risk even if it was poorly installed.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC furnace safety material emphasizes flue blockages and combustion byproducts, not just whether heat turns on.
cases.deal: Buyer thinks the furnace is fine because it warmed the house.
findings: orphaned water heater vent into oversized chimney
cases.requiredGate: do not equate operation with safe venting
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may miss carbon monoxide or backdrafting risk because the appliance operated briefly.

cases.sourceBasis: ENERGY STAR guidance identifies duct leakage and airflow as performance defects, which can matter even when the equipment itself runs.
cases.deal: One bedroom is unusably hot during inspection walkthrough.
findings: no airflow at rear bedroom register
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may ask for a fan while ignoring the failed conditioned-air delivery.

cases.sourceBasis: HVAC safety and inspection standards distinguish inaccessible or untested systems from passed systems.
cases.deal: Closing is in five days and heating could not be tested because fuel was off.
findings: oil boiler not operated during inspection
cases.requiredGate: untested system must not be marked cleared
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer closes with no proof the primary heat source is safe or functional.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards include permanently installed heating and cooling equipment, but not seller promises about future servicing.
cases.deal: Seller offers a home warranty instead of HVAC repair.
findings: heat pump auxiliary heat not operating
cases.requiredGate: known defect not solved by vague warranty
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer accepts warranty language that may exclude a known pre-existing HVAC defect.

cases.sourceBasis: HVAC and moisture guidance links failed condensate management to water damage and mold-like staining.
cases.deal: AS IS condo has air handler in a closet above finished flooring.
findings: water stain below air handler closet
cases.requiredGate: moisture source and HOA responsibility check
cases.riskIfWrong: The request may chase cosmetic flooring damage without addressing the condensate leak.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection standards require reporting active plumbing leaks observed during inspection.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a small credit for many minor plumbing notes.
findings: active leak at kitchen sink trap
cases.riskIfWrong: The valid leak gets diluted into a cosmetic kitchen update request.

cases.sourceBasis: Polybutylene public real estate guidance treats pipe presence, leak history, and insurance availability as separate risk checks.
cases.deal: Inspection found PB piping in a 1994 subdivision home.
findings: polybutylene supply piping visible in crawlspace
past ceiling patch below upstairs bath
cases.requiredGate: insurance and plumber confirmation before ask amount
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may either ignore PB as not leaking or overstate failure without quote and insurance evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance underwriting sources show active leaks and plumbing material risks can block coverage, especially in four-point markets.
cases.deal: Buyer needs insurance approval before AS IS inspection period expires.
findings: polybutylene pipes at water heater closet
active leak at tub valve access panel
expectedLeadScope: water heater age and leak risk
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may negotiate repairs that still leave the home uninsurable.

cases.sourceBasis: Plumbing leaks require source repair before concealed moisture damage can be scoped.
cases.deal: Condo inspection found moisture at a shared wall.
findings: moisture meter elevated behind hall bath
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet asks only for interior patching and misses shared building or neighbor damage exposure.

cases.sourceBasis: Inspection and insurance sources treat old water heaters with leaks or unsafe discharge as more than appliance age.
cases.deal: Seller says the water heater works and age is not negotiable.
findings: water heater tank actively leaking at base
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may wrongly demote the issue as age-only instead of active failure.

cases.sourceBasis: Plumbing material and hidden leak risks are different from fixture finish preferences.
cases.deal: Investor wants seller to fund a bathroom remodel after inspection.
findings: galvanized supply pipes with low flow
cases.riskIfWrong: The ask becomes a renovation credit rather than a defensible plumbing repair.

cases.sourceBasis: Water intrusion research emphasizes identifying whether the source is plumbing, roof, or exterior drainage before remediating damage.
cases.deal: Finished basement has staining after a recent bathroom remodel.
findings: new shower pan lacks visible permit
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer could ask for repainting while a failed shower pan continues leaking.

cases.sourceBasis: Public inspection standards require reporting active water leaks but not predicting every concealed pipe defect.
cases.deal: Agent draft claims all copper plumbing must be replaced due to one pinhole leak.
findings: one active pinhole leak at copper elbow
expectedExclusions: entire system failed without plumber test
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet overstates visible evidence and becomes easy for the seller to attack.

cases.sourceBasis: Sump pump and foundation drainage problems are system risks when they control below-grade water entry.
cases.deal: Home has a finished basement and no backup power at the sump.
findings: minor carpet wear in guest room
expectedExclusions: minor carpet wear in guest room
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may close on a finished basement whose only drainage protection is not working.

cases.sourceBasis: Plumbing leak evidence and water damage should be linked to repair quality and reinspection before closing.
cases.deal: Seller says the plumber fixed the leak yesterday but no invoice is attached.
findings: fresh caulk under sink after prior active leak
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may accept a concealed wet cabinet and undocumented repair.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA and CDC mold cleanup guidance centers moisture control and complete cleanup rather than naming species from visual inspection.
cases.deal: Inspection report says mold-like staining in the attic after a roof leak.
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may make unsupported environmental claims or miss the moisture condition that causes recurrence.

cases.sourceBasis: Mold cleanup resources emphasize that cleanup without fixing leaks or moisture will fail.
cases.deal: Seller offers to bleach visible staining before closing.
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer accepts stain removal while the leak continues behind the wall.

cases.sourceBasis: CDC public guidance links mold growth to moisture around roofs, windows, pipes, and flooding, requiring source-specific follow-up.
cases.deal: Buyer is alarmed by black staining but no lab test exists.
findings: black mold-like staining under kitchen sink
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet could either panic the buyer with unsupported toxicity claims or underplay a live moisture issue.

cases.sourceBasis: Water intrusion and mold-like staining in crawlspaces should be tied to drainage, vapor, and wood condition rather than cosmetic cleanup.
cases.deal: Crawlspace company quote arrives after inspection but before objection deadline.
cases.riskIfWrong: The request may accept an upsold appliance without correcting water entry and vapor conditions.

cases.sourceBasis: Mold and moisture sources require deciding whether the problem is roof, plumbing, HVAC condensate, or exterior intrusion.
cases.deal: Condo seller says staining is an HOA roof matter and refuses interior repair.
findings: mold-like staining at ceiling below roof deck
HOA roof leak work order open
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may ask the wrong party for roof work or ignore interior damage the seller controls.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA mold cleanup guidance supports specialist involvement for larger or recurring contamination and prioritizes preventing re-growth.
cases.deal: Basement remediation quote is large and seller offers a small credit.
findings: mold-like staining over multiple basement walls
old sump pump with no lid
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may accept a token credit for a recurring moisture and remediation problem.

cases.sourceBasis: Moisture staining without elevated moisture or source evidence should be framed differently from active intrusion.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for mold remediation after a dry stain in a desert home.
findings: old dry stain at ceiling corner
roof patch invoice from five years ago
buyer asks for whole-house mold remediation
expectedExclusions: whole-house mold remediation without active evidence
cases.requiredGate: do not convert dry stain into broad remediation ask
cases.riskIfWrong: The system validates an unsupported environmental demand.

cases.sourceBasis: Mold-like staining around HVAC or ducts should connect to condensation, insulation, and airflow conditions.
cases.deal: Inspection was performed during humid weather with AC running.
expectedExclusions: dirty return filter as standalone major ask
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may request cleaning while missing the condensation condition causing recurrence.

cases.sourceBasis: Deck safety resources prioritize ledger attachment, flashing, fasteners, stairs, guards, and decay over surface appearance.
cases.deal: Elevated deck overlooks a slope and seller says it was built by prior owner.
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may treat an elevated deck collapse risk like normal deck maintenance.

cases.sourceBasis: NADRA deck evaluation materials distinguish decay, corroded fasteners, stairs, and guards from cosmetic deck finish.
cases.deal: Junior agent wants to ask for full deck replacement and landscaping cleanup.
expectedExclusions: full deck replacement without structural scope
cases.riskIfWrong: Seller can dismiss the ask as beautification instead of recognizing occupant-safety defects.

cases.sourceBasis: Chimney safety guidance treats cracked flue liners, creosote evidence, and masonry damage as fire-safety issues requiring specialist evaluation.
cases.deal: Home has a wood-burning fireplace the buyer plans to use immediately.
findings: cracked flue tile noted by chimney scan
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may treat the fireplace as usable and negotiate only cosmetic hearth updates.

cases.sourceBasis: Chimney and roof flashing sources show water entry at masonry penetrations can damage both roof assemblies and interior finishes.
cases.deal: Seller had chimney tuckpointed but attic still shows staining.
findings: attic water stain adjacent to chimney
cases.requiredGate: invoice does not cover observed leak source
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may accept masonry paperwork that does not address roof water entry.

cases.sourceBasis: CPSC pool barrier guidance prioritizes self-closing/self-latching gates and door alarms where the house opens to the pool.
cases.deal: AS IS home with pool and child-safety concerns.
findings: rear slider opens directly to pool with no alarm
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may miss a child-safety hazard and focus on pool appearance.

cases.sourceBasis: Pool electrical safety resources separate pump operation from grounding, bonding, and GFCI protection.
cases.deal: Pool inspector says the equipment runs but electrical safety is incomplete.
cases.requiredGate: operation does not clear electrical safety
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may accept working pool equipment while electrocution protection is unresolved.

cases.sourceBasis: Deck standards emphasize guard and handrail stability because falls are a life-safety risk.
cases.deal: Mountain property has a second-story balcony deck.
findings: deck guard spacing is wide enough for child passage
guard posts move under hand pressure
cases.requiredGate: fall hazard evidence and specialist quote
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may negotiate furniture or finish items while a fall hazard remains.

cases.sourceBasis: Chimney safety guidance recommends professional evaluation after signs of chimney fire or damaged liner.
cases.deal: Buyer requests a complete chimney rebuild after a level-one visual inspection.
expectedExclusions: full rebuild without camera or mason scope
cases.riskIfWrong: The request skips needed evidence and inflates scope beyond the inspection finding.

cases.sourceBasis: Pool barrier guidance treats above-ground access ladders and gates as part of child access control.
cases.deal: Home has an above-ground pool the seller plans to leave.
findings: above-ground pool ladder cannot be locked
cases.requiredGate: pool safety item or remove pool before closing
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may treat a removable pool as personal property and miss a liability hazard.

cases.sourceBasis: Deck inspection resources flag ledgers attached to masonry veneer or inaccessible structural connections as needing design-professional review.
cases.deal: Brick veneer home has a large attached deck with finished ceiling below.
findings: deck ledger appears attached through brick veneer
expectedLeadScope: design professional or deck contractor review
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may falsely clear a critical deck connection that was not visible.

cases.sourceBasis: WDI guidance links wood-to-ground contact, moisture, and mud tubes to termite risk requiring pest specialist evaluation.
cases.deal: Termite letter is not yet ordered and inspection shows conducive conditions.
findings: termite mud tubes on foundation pier
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may miss active infestation or hidden structural damage during the contingency period.

cases.sourceBasis: NC WDI public guidance clarifies that WDI reports cover more than termites and note conducive moisture and cellulose conditions.
cases.deal: Buyer has high due diligence money and wants to know whether to walk.
findings: wood moisture content reported above 20 percent in crawlspace
cases.riskIfWrong: The system may separate pest and moisture issues that must be handled together.

cases.sourceBasis: Termite prevention guidance identifies wood-to-soil contact as a common access path and moisture as a conducive condition.
cases.deal: Buyer requests all floor joists be replaced after seeing old termite tubes.
findings: no visible joist damage in accessible area
cases.riskIfWrong: The request jumps from evidence of risk to unsupported structural replacement.

cases.sourceBasis: WDI and crawlspace sources show pest damage should be paired with structural evaluation when load-bearing wood is affected.
cases.deal: Pest inspector confirms active termites after the general inspection.
findings: damaged sill plate at rear crawlspace
cases.requiredGate: pest treatment plus structural repair quote
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer might ask only for treatment and miss damaged load-bearing wood.

cases.sourceBasis: Termite guidance warns surface treatment alone may not solve below-ground entry or moisture conditions.
cases.deal: Seller provides a receipt for a spot spray after WDI report.
findings: seller receipt says spot treatment only
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may accept a minimal treatment receipt while the conducive leak remains.

cases.sourceBasis: WDI reports can find fungi, dry rot, beetles, and carpenter ants in addition to termites, so the packet should not collapse everything into termite treatment.
cases.deal: Pest report identifies fungus damage at a deck and eaves.
findings: fungus damage at deck joist ends
dry rot at fascia near gutter leak
cases.requiredGate: correct WDI category and source control
cases.riskIfWrong: The request asks for the wrong pest remedy and ignores moisture-driven wood decay.

cases.sourceBasis: WDI inspection reports are limited to accessible evidence, so hidden damage risk must be framed as uncertainty, not certainty.
cases.deal: Seller remodeled basement walls before listing and WDI access was limited.
findings: old termite treatment sticker in basement
cases.riskIfWrong: Packet may overpromise hidden damage findings or falsely clear inaccessible areas.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance four-point reviews evaluate roof, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC together, so multiple moderate defects can combine into quote failure.
cases.deal: Buyer has three days left in AS IS inspection period and no firm binder.
findings: older shingle roof with unknown remaining life
expectedExclusions: AC replacement because unit cools adequately
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may spend the deadline negotiating credits that cannot produce an insurable closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Quote-needed risks are highest when inspection evidence identifies a serious system defect but no trade scope or repair method exists.
cases.deal: Objection deadline is tomorrow and only the general inspection is complete.
cases.riskIfWrong: The system invents a single ask number across unpriced structural, sewer, and electrical risks.

cases.sourceBasis: Major systems should be prioritized by safety, active failure, financing, and insurability rather than number of report bullets.
cases.deal: High-volume team wants a QA case for reducing a 90-item report.
cases.requiredGate: scope discipline under long report pressure
cases.riskIfWrong: The product becomes a prettier inspection report summary instead of a negotiation triage tool.

cases.sourceBasis: Lender-visible repair risks differ from buyer preference items and should be gated when FHA or VA financing is involved.
cases.deal: VA buyer has safety and sanitation defects in inspection before appraisal.
findings: active roof leak over electrical fixture
expectedLeadScope: active roof leak over electrical fixture
cases.requiredGate: VA/lender confirmation and repair completion caveat
cases.riskIfWrong: The packet may present credit language for items that could require completion before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller-side pushback is strongest when valid system defects are mixed with upgrades, cosmetics, and speculative future replacements.
cases.deal: Listing side wants to classify buyer request items for counteroffer.
findings: active plumbing leak at crawlspace supply
cases.riskIfWrong: The seller may reject even valid repairs because the product endorses a mixed wishlist.

cases.sourceBasis: Expired contingency or option windows can make even serious defects advisory rather than sendable repair requests.
cases.deal: Option period expired yesterday and buyer just received sewer scope video.
findings: seller has not agreed to extend option
expectedExclusions: normal first repair demand after expired option
cases.riskIfWrong: The system may draft a normal repair request after the buyer's strongest leverage expired.

cases.sourceBasis: Repair receipts and seller promises require verification for critical systems before final walk-through or closing.
cases.deal: Closing is tomorrow and seller says all serious items are complete.
findings: roof leak repair receipt lacks photos
electrical panel repair invoice missing permit
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer closes after relying on paperwork that does not prove critical defects were resolved.

cases.sourceBasis: General inspection limitations mean underground, concealed, and inaccessible components often need specialist follow-up instead of definitive clearance.
cases.deal: Inspector wants output that respects inspection scope limitations.
findings: crawlspace inaccessible due to low clearance
agent asks for clean pass language
cases.riskIfWrong: The tool creates false certainty about systems the inspector did not inspect.

cases.sourceBasis: Cost and credit strategy should not exceed usable lender or contract pathways when repairs are safety or collateral sensitive.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for a large seller credit on an FHA file.
findings: buyer wants all items handled as closing cost credit
cases.riskIfWrong: The request may negotiate an unusable credit for items the lender wants repaired.

cases.sourceBasis: Multiple water sources require separating roof, plumbing, and site drainage before assigning a single repair scope.
cases.deal: Historic rowhouse has stains in several locations with different likely causes.
findings: front bedroom ceiling stain below roof parapet
cases.requiredGate: separate water sources and trade scopes
cases.riskIfWrong: A single generic water-damage credit may be underpriced and impossible to defend.

cases.sourceBasis: Buyer market leverage can justify stronger asks, but scope should still be anchored to major system defects.
cases.deal: Property has been listed for 120 days and seller is motivated.
findings: failed sewer scope due to broken clay pipe
cases.requiredGate: strong ask but no cosmetic drift
cases.riskIfWrong: The product either underuses leverage or weakens the request with cosmetic extras.

cases.sourceBasis: Competitive seller markets require minimal, defensible asks focused on defects that could threaten safety, financing, or insurance.
cases.deal: Seller has backup offers and says no repairs unless safety related.
findings: active roof leak at vent boot
cases.riskIfWrong: Buyer may lose the deal by including age and preference items alongside true safety defects.

cases.sourceBasis: Quote-needed cases should preserve uncertainty when defect severity is known but repair method is unknown.
cases.deal: Seller requests a dollar number today but specialists cannot visit until tomorrow.
cases.requiredGate: do not invent unquoted repair amount
cases.riskIfWrong: The output may produce a confident but fictional credit number across three specialist scopes.

cases.sourceBasis: Post-counter workflows require comparing seller cure quality to the original system risk, not drafting a brand-new first ask.
cases.deal: Inspection objection was sent and seller countered with selected repairs.
findings: seller refuses sewer root intrusion credit
seller offers to clean mold-like crawlspace staining
cases.riskIfWrong: The system ignores workflow state and drafts demands that do not fit the pending resolution deadline.

cases.sourceBasis: Physical system triage should create an immediate, copy-ready packet while preserving caveats for quotes, lenders, insurance, and specialist scopes.
cases.persona: SEO landing-page visitor with live deal
cases.deal: Visitor searched for help turning a 55-page inspection report into a seller credit request.
cases.requiredGate: immediate output with quote-needed and insurance caveats
cases.riskIfWrong: User gets a generic article or bloated wishlist instead of a usable high-risk negotiation packet.
